rightsizing_log.test: T1 — one coherent thing per session
rightsizing_log.finding: Title contains a coordinating conjunction ('&') joining two primary verbs — validation and provisioning. Two nameable objectives, one unit.
rightsizing_log.resolution: Split into WU-F5.1-02 (OIDC token validation, 3 pts) and a role-provisioning remainder (2 pts). Points preserved at 5.
rightsizing_log.note: Appendix B.2 of the BOM offers this exact title as a T1-compliant example. The encoded check disagrees with the illustration; the check is what runs.

draft_units: role-provisioning remainder from the T1 split (2 pts)
rightsizing_log.finding: Both units resolve a role from the same onboarding record and neither is verifiable in isolation — the mapping unit has no observable behaviour until provisioning writes a role, and provisioning has nothing to write until the mapping exists. Each named the other as a hard dependency.
rightsizing_log.resolution: Merged into WU-F5.1-03 (Role provisioning from the onboarding record, 5 pts), verified by TC-F5.1-02.
rightsizing_log.note: The T1 split produced a fragment too small to stand alone. T1 and T5 pull against each other by design, and the resolution is a unit that is one coherent thing AND independently verifiable — not the smallest possible piece.

rightsizing_log.finding: est_files_read 17 against a ceiling of 12; est_context_tokens 108,000 against a ceiling of 100,000 (0.5 x a 200k window). The unit needed the producer schema, the OpenAPI contract, the validation rules and the UI wireframe simultaneously.
rightsizing_log.resolution: Split on the natural data/api seam into WU-F1.1-01 (Producer entity schema migration, data, 3 pts) and WU-F1.1-02 (FBO number capture endpoint, api, 5 pts). Post-split: 4 and 9 files read, 19k and 52k tokens. Points preserved at 8.
rightsizing_log.note: T2 counts files READ, not files changed. The draft changed few files and read many, which is the case the test exists to catch.

rightsizing_log.finding: verification_ref was empty. No unit ships without a named verifier.
rightsizing_log.resolution: Bound to TC-S-F1.1-b-01 (valid lookup against a stubbed register) and TC-S-F1.1-b-03 (timeout leaves the registration pending).
rightsizing_log.note: The verifier existed already — case-writer minted it before this agent ran. T3 failing here was a binding omission, not a missing test.

rightsizing_log.finding: On the re-run, verification_ref named TC-S-F1.1-b-99 for the duplicate-delivery behaviour. No such case_id exists in the minted set. gr-L1-verification-ref-resolvable blocked the unit.
rightsizing_log.resolution: Corrected to TC-ADV-S-F1.1-b-01, the adversarial case that actually covers duplicate verification delivery.
rightsizing_log.note: A non-empty verification_ref is not the same as a resolvable one. A plausible-looking case id is the failure mode this guardrail exists for — it would have shipped a Work Unit whose verifier nobody could run.

rightsizing_log.finding: Registration submission form spans ui and api: client-side validation mirrors the contract WU-F1.1-02 owns.
rightsizing_log.resolution: NOT SPLIT. Carried as a warning in reflection_notes for the evaluator.
rightsizing_log.rationale: Splitting would produce a form unit with no validation and a validation unit with no form, neither independently demonstrable. The mirroring is intentional — the server remains authoritative (TC-ADV-S-F1.1-a-01 proves a forged client-side flag is ignored), and the client copy is a usability affordance, not a second enforcement point. T4 is WARN precisely because some layer-spanning units are legitimate.

capacity_signal.note: This agent does not assign cycle or disposition — those are L1-planning-feature-cycle-planner's fields. The signal is raised because the fit invariant (sum of committed unit_points <= capacity) is the planner's to enforce and gr-L1-consistency-check will reject an over-committed cycle. Overflow units must carry disposition=overflow with a reflow_band, never be silently dropped. The natural candidate is S-F1.1-b (WU-F1.1-05, WU-F1.1-06, 8 pts), since the slice sequencing already places it after S-F1.1-a.

reflection_notes: T4 WARN on WU-F1.1-03 carried unactioned with rationale — for the evaluator, not silently swallowed.
WU-F1.1-02 sits exactly at the T5 hard-dependency ceiling of 2. Worth watching if the endpoint grows.

OQ-01 and OQ-02 from story-generator remain open. Neither blocks a Cycle 1 Work Unit: OQ-02 (live register vs cached copy) shapes WU-F1.1-05's implementation but not its existence or its verifier, and the unit is written against a stubbed register either way.

content.execution_summary:
• Emitted 9 Work Units across F5.1 (3 units, 13 pts) and F1.1 (6 units across 2 slices, 22 pts). Every unit carries a layer from the enum and at least one verification_ref that resolves to a minted case_id.
• Right-sizing did real work: 6 events, 4 of them blocking. T1 blocked 'OIDC token validation & role provisioning' on its conjunction and split it; T5 then merged the 2-point remainder back with the role-mapping draft, because the split had produced a fragment nothing could verify alone. T2 blocked a unit reading 17 files and 108k tokens, splitting it on the data/api seam. T3 blocked the FBO lookup unit twice — once for an empty verification_ref, once for TC-S-F1.1-b-99, a plausible-looking case id that does not exist.
• The second T3 block is the one worth reading: a non-empty verifier reference is not a resolvable one, and gr-L1-verification-ref-resolvable is what stands between a Work Unit and a verifier nobody can run.
• T4 WARN on WU-F1.1-03 was carried, not actioned. Splitting the registration form from its client-side validation would leave neither half demonstrable, and the server stays authoritative — TC-ADV-S-F1.1-a-01 proves a forged client flag is ignored. T4 is WARN because some layer-spanning units are legitimate.
• Verifier coverage: all 14 minted case_ids are claimed by at least one Work Unit; no unit claims a case id that does not exist.
• Capacity: 35 points emitted against 30. Flagged to L1-planning-feature-cycle-planner rather than resolved here — cycle and disposition are the planner's fields, and overflow units must carry disposition=overflow with a reflow_band rather than being dropped. S-F1.1-b (8 pts) is the natural overflow candidate on the existing slice sequencing.
• Knowledge bases consulted: kb-L1-decomposition-standard (T1–T5, the layer enum, N=12 and 0.5 x window defaults — not overridden); kb-L1-sdlc-templates (Work Unit record shape).
• Guardrails evaluated: gr-L1-schema-validator (pass), gr-L1-decomposition-rightsizing (pass after 4 blocking corrections; 2 warnings carried), gr-L1-verification-ref-resolvable (pass after 1 correction).
• Over-decomposition was actively resisted: the governing rule is the coarsest level that is still independently verifiable and context-bounded, and the T5 merge is the evidence that the rule was applied in both directions rather than only downward.
